items.title: Seeking Out Aspiration, Lineage, Faculty, and Conduct — Four Loci, Four Methods

items.zh: 如是問已，彼若云：爾！次後復於四種處所，以四因緣應正尋求。何等名為四種處所？一、應尋求其願，二、應尋求種姓，三、應尋求其根，四、應尋求其行。云何名為四種因緣？一、應以審問而正尋求；二、應以言論而正尋求；三、應以所作而正尋求；四、應以知他心差別智而正尋求。
items.en: Having asked thus, if the seeker answers affirmatively, the teacher should next rightly seek out four matters through four means. What are the four matters? First, one should seek out his aspiration. Second, one should seek out his spiritual lineage. Third, one should seek out his faculty. Fourth, one should seek out his conduct. What are the four means? First, one should rightly seek through interrogation. Second, one should rightly seek through discourse. Third, one should rightly seek through observed conduct. Fourth, one should rightly seek through the wisdom that discerns another's mind.

items.zh: 云何名為應以審問尋求其願？
謂如是問：長老！於何以發正願？聲聞乘耶？獨覺乘耶？無上正等菩提乘耶？彼得此問，隨自所願，當如是答。如是名為應以審問尋求其願。
items.en: That is, one asks thus: "Elder! Towards which have you set your correct aspiration — the Hearer's vehicle? The Solitary Realiser's vehicle? Or the vehicle of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment?" Receiving this question, the seeker answers according to his own aspiration. This is called rightly seeking out his aspiration through interrogation.

items.zh: 云何名為應以審問尋求種姓及以根行？謂如是問：長老！於自種姓、根、行能審察不？謂我本來有何種姓？聲聞乘耶？獨覺乘耶？大乘等耶？有何等根？為鈍？為中？為利根耶？有何等行？為貪行耶？為瞋行耶？廣說乃至尋思行耶？彼若黠慧，能自了知前後差別種姓、根、行，善取其相，如問而答。若性愚鈍，不能自知前後差別，乃至不能善取其相，由是不能如問而答。從此已後，應以言論尋求彼三。

items.title: Section: Discerning Lineage Through Discourse — Three Vehicles, Three Reactions

items.zh: 謂對其前，應以顯了正理相應眾雜美妙易解言詞，說聲聞乘相應言論。彼聞宣說此言論時，若身中有聲聞種姓，於此言論便發最極踴躍歡喜，深生信解。若身中有獨覺種姓、大乘種姓，於此言論不發最極踊躍歡喜，不生信解。次復為其說獨覺乘相應言論。彼聞宣說此言論時，若身中有獨覺種姓，於此言論便發最極踊躍歡喜，深生信解。若身中有聲聞種姓、大乘種姓，則不如是。後復為其宣說大乘相應言論。
items.en: That is, before the seeker, one should speak, with clear, principle-aligned, well-ordered, beautiful, and easily understood words, a discourse corresponding to the Hearer's vehicle. When he hears this discourse, if he has the Hearer's lineage within him, he gives rise to the utmost leaping joy over this discourse and deep confidence and understanding. If he has the Solitary Realiser's or Great Vehicle's lineage within him, he does not give rise to such utmost joy, nor such confidence and understanding regarding it. Next, one speaks to him a discourse corresponding to the Solitary Realiser's vehicle … And afterwards, one speaks to him a discourse corresponding to the Great Vehicle …

items.zh: 彼聞宣說此言論時，若身中有大乘種姓，於此言論、便發最極踊躍歡喜，深生信解。若身中有聲聞種姓、獨覺種姓，則不如是。

items.title: Discerning Faculty and the Five Kinds of Conduct Through Discourse

items.zh: 若有鈍根，雖聞宣說麁淺言論，而於法義勵力審思，方能領受解了通達。若有利根，雖聞宣說深細言論，而於法義速能領受解了通達。若有中根，則不如是。
items.en: If he has a dull faculty, then even hearing a coarse and shallow discourse, he must still labour and reflect carefully upon its meaning before he can receive, understand, and penetrate it. If he has a sharp faculty, then even hearing a deep and subtle discourse, he can swiftly receive, understand, and penetrate its meaning. If he has a middling faculty, it is neither of these.

items.zh: 若有貪行，彼聞為說淨妙言論，便發最極淨信愛樂，悟入其趣；身毛皆竪，悲涕墮淚；其身外現潤滑相狀，其心內懷柔軟怡悅。若有瞋行，當知一切與上相違。若有癡行，彼聞為說決定通達涅槃離染相應言論，便生最極驚恐怖畏。如說鈍根，如是癡行，當知亦爾。若有慢行，彼聞為說正法言論，不甚恭敬屬耳樂聞，不極安住求欲領解奉教行心。雖作方便引發其心，令受正化，而不分明發言稱善。若尋思行，彼聞為說正法言論，雖攝耳聽，而心散亂，惡受所受。凡所領受不堅不住，隨受隨失，數重請問。
items.en: If his conduct is dominated by craving, then hearing a discourse on giving, precepts, and heavenly rebirth, he gives rise to the utmost pure faith and delight, awakening into its meaning — his body hair standing on end, tears of emotion falling. If his conduct is dominated by hatred, know that everything is the reverse of this. If his conduct is dominated by delusion, then hearing a discourse establishing, with certainty, the penetration of nirvāṇa and freedom from defilement, he gives rise to the utmost fright and terror. If his conduct is dominated by pride, then hearing a discourse on the true Dharma, he does not listen with much reverence or delight. And if his conduct is dominated by discursive thought, then hearing a discourse on the true Dharma, though he strains to listen, his mind is scattered — what he grasps he grasps wrongly, and whatever he receives neither stays firm nor abides, being lost as soon as it is gained, so that he must ask the same question again and again.

items.zh: 如是名為應以言論尋求種姓及以根、行。云何名為應以所作尋求彼三？

items.title: Discerning Through Observed Conduct and Through Reading the Mind Directly

items.zh: 謂如前說聲聞種姓，及貪等行補特伽羅所有相狀，是名所作。由此所作，如其所應，當正尋求種、姓、根行。云何名為應以知他心差別智尋求種姓及以根、行？謂如有一善達瑜伽修瑜伽師，以得知他心差別智。彼由如是他心智故，如實了知種性、根、行。
items.en: That is, the marks belonging to one of the Hearer's lineage, and to individuals of craving-dominated conduct and the rest, as previously explained, are called "observed conduct." Through such observed conduct, one should rightly seek out lineage, faculty, and conduct as is fitting. … That is, suppose there is a teacher well versed in yogic practice who has already attained the wisdom that discerns another's mind. Through this mind-reading wisdom, he truly and accurately knows the seeker's lineage, faculty, and conduct.

blocks.text: How a teacher finds out what kind of person is in front of them, before choosing a practice. A short passage (0449a27) is untranslated.

The teacher seeks out four things: the seeker's **aspiration**, **lineage**, **faculty**, and **conduct**. By four means: by asking, by discourse, by observing conduct, and "through the wisdom that discerns another's mind". Master Cháng Bǎi: a teacher with that wisdom needs no other method.
"Towards which have you set your aspiration: the hearer's vehicle, the solitary realiser's, or unsurpassed awakening?"

The teacher speaks "with clear, well-ordered, beautiful, easily understood words" a discourse matching the hearer's vehicle. "If he has the hearer's lineage, he gives rise to the utmost joy and deep confidence." Then a discourse on the solitary realiser's vehicle; then on the great vehicle. The listener's response shows the lineage.

"If he has a dull faculty, even hearing a coarse and shallow discourse, he must labour to understand it." A middling faculty: "neither of these". A craving-type, hearing a discourse on giving, precepts, and heaven, "gives rise to the utmost faith and delight". A delusion-type responds to teachings on dependent origination with confusion; "whatever he receives does not stay, lost as soon as gained, so that he must ask the same thing again".
The marks of temperament described on Days 221–222 are "observed conduct". A teacher with mind-reading knows directly.

quiz.q: What four matters should be sought out, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi say the teacher observes?
options: aspiration, lineage, faculty, conduct; observing what the seeker's body does, speech says, mind shows
quiz.why: "First, one should seek out his aspiration. Second, his spiritual lineage. Third, his faculty. Fourth, his conduct." Master Cháng Bǎi: the teacher observes what the seeker displays — what the body does, what speech says, how the mind reacts.

quiz.q: The fourth means is "the wisdom that discerns another's mind." What do the masters say?
options: both: a teacher with mind-reading enters absorption and knows — Cháng Bǎi adds, even whether the seeker lies
quiz.why: "Fourth, one should rightly seek through the wisdom that discerns another's mind." Master Cháng Bǎi: a teacher with mind-reading enters absorption to observe, and can tell whether the seeker is lying. Venerable Miào Jìng: he simply enters absorption and observes with mind-reading — then he knows.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "body" in "if he has the Hearer's lineage within his body"?
options: body means mind — inseparable from it, the mind holds the Hearer's seeds
quiz.why: "If he has the Hearer's lineage within him, he gives rise to the utmost leaping joy over this discourse and deep confidence and understanding." Master Cháng Bǎi: "body" here means the mind — body is inseparable from mind, and the mind holds the Hearer's seeds.

quiz.q: Besides dull and sharp faculties, "a middling faculty is neither." How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe it?
options: may not grasp at first, but understands with a bit more explanation
quiz.why: "If he has a middling faculty, it is neither of these." Master Cháng Bǎi: at first perhaps not very clear, but with a bit more explanation he understands.

quiz.q: Craving types delight in "淨妙言論," rendered "a discourse on giving, precepts, and heavenly rebirth." What example does Venerable Miào Jìng give?
options: Amitābha's land adorned with seven jewels; the English "giving, precepts, heaven" comes from the Pixunji, not the text
quiz.why: "If his conduct is dominated by craving, then hearing a discourse on giving, precepts, and heavenly rebirth, he gives rise to the utmost pure faith and delight." Venerable Miào Jìng: e.g., telling of Amitābha's land adorned with seven jewels, its environment and inhabitants all splendid. The English specifics come from the Pixunji; the text says only "pure, wondrous discourse."

quiz.q: Delusion types are terrified by "a discourse establishing with certainty …" How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "certainty"?
options: by impermanence — teachings that formations are certainly impermanent
quiz.why: "If his conduct is dominated by delusion, then hearing a discourse establishing, with certainty, the penetration of nirvāṇa and freedom from defilement, he gives rise to the utmost fright and terror." Master Cháng Bǎi: by the sense of impermanence — "certainty" means teachings that formations are certainly impermanent.

quiz.q: Seeking through "observed conduct." What does Venerable Miào Jìng call "observed conduct"?
options: such lineage, faculties, and afflictions show themselves in such marks
quiz.why: "The marks belonging to one of the Hearer's lineage, and to individuals of craving-dominated conduct and the rest, as previously explained, are called 'observed conduct.'" Venerable Miào Jìng: having such a lineage, sharp or dull faculties, and such afflictions, he displays such marks — that is "observed conduct."
